subject: RTBF requirements: backup snapshot windows & deletion authorization (post-demo recap)
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel@brightwave.health>, Elena Soto <elena@brightwave.health>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RTBF requirements: backup snapshot windows & deletion authorization (post-demo recap)

Hi Daniel / Elena —

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap and the follow-ups we promised on RTBF/delete flows for records that may appear in backups/snapshots. I pulled this together based on the architecture discussion and what we covered with Soojin on the call.

Key points from the call:
- Scope: user PII in service logs, text-based message content, and derived embeddings.
- Primary requirement: ability to process customer-initiated deletion requests (RTBF) that remove material data from live stores within 7 business days, with an additional hard-delete window for asynchronous backups.
- Backup constraint you called out: daily EBS-style snapshots retained for 30 days, some infra snapshots are immutable for compliance until a 30-day retention policy completes.

Action items we agreed: 
1) Redwood to confirm what we can guarantee for live-store deletions vs snapshots and provide a recommended purge timeline.
2) Customer to share procurement/infosec clause that mandates immutable snapshot retention vs acceptable soft-delete windows.
3) Follow-up: Soojin and I will pull together a short RTBF checklist and a proposed legal-friendly paragraph that maps to your procurement terms.

Attached: RTBF checklist draft and a snapshot retention matrix (working draft).

Open questions we need to clarify from your side: 
- Which workflows allow BrightWave to request overwrite vs do-you-require evidence-of-destruction?
- Are there specific backup stores (cloud region snapshots, S3 lifecycle archives) that are considered subject to the retention you mentioned?

Next steps:
- We (Redwood) will propose a two-phase purge: live-store purge within 7 business days; best-effort snapshot purge notification + a recommended scheduling window for custodial overwrites.
- Proposed time for follow-up call: Thu 30 Sep or Mon 4 Oct.

If that aligns, we’ll get a short one-page legal-friendly paragraph back to you for procurement.

Thanks,
Marcus
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
attachments: rtbf-checklist-v1.pdf (application/pdf), snapshot-retention-matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Daniel Park <daniel@brightwave.health>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Soto <elena@brightwave.health>, procurement@brightwave.health
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RTBF requirements: backup snapshot windows & deletion authorization (post-demo recap)

Thanks Marcus — useful summary. Couple clarifications from our side: 

1) BrightWave requires proof that PII removal requests are honored in the live system within 7 business days. For backups, our legal team accepts a "best-effort purge" model if we receive a written plan + schedule for snapshot overwrites or deletions within 45 days. Immutable backups created for regulatory audits (we've got a small subset tagged: audit-retain) are a different conversation — we will list those explicitly in the procurement doc.

2) For evidence, procurement prefers a short attestation statement signed by the vendor (Redwood) and a copy of the purge job logs where possible. A redacted example is fine.

3) We maintain some cross-region cold archives (S3 Glacier) where deletion can take longer due to lifecycle transitions. Please call out limits for those.

We can do Thu 30 Sep at 10:00 PT to review the proposed paragraph and the checklist.

—Daniel
Director, InfoSec | BrightWave Health

Marcus — forwarding Daniel's note. I'm drafting the legal-friendly paragraph now. A few internal points to decide before we send anything to procurement: 

- We should differentiate three tiers in the paragraph: live-store deletion (guaranteed within X days), short-term snapshot windows (best-effort overwrite within Y days), and immutable audit snapshots (explicitly excluded and listed).
- Default Y we can offer: 45 days for snapshot overwrite unless customer provides an explicit exception. This maps to common procurement asks and keeps operational complexity bounded.
- Evidence/attestation: we can provide a redacted purge log + signed attestation. Note: logs will contain request IDs, timestamps, and job outcomes; we can redact user identifiers in attestation.

I attached an internal checklist with possible wording and a sample attestation format. Marcus — do you want me to produce two variants (45-day and 30-day) so procurement can choose?

—Soojin
Privacy & Compliance Manager | Redwood Inference

Daniel / Elena —

Thanks for the clear outline. Per our internal discussion we've produced two short options below (language ready for procurement):

Option A (45-day snapshot overwrite window):
"Redwood Inference will remove customer-designated personal data from live production stores within seven (7) business days of a valid request. For backups and system-level snapshots, Redwood will execute overwrite or deletion procedures on a best-effort basis and will complete such operations within forty-five (45) calendar days unless a snapshot is explicitly tagged as "audit-retain" in which case the snapshot will be handled according to mutually-agreed exception procedures. Redwood will provide a redacted purge log and a signed attestation upon completion of deletion activities."

Option B (30-day snapshot overwrite window):
"Redwood Inference will remove customer-designated personal data from live production stores within seven (7) business days of a valid request. For backups and system-level snapshots, Redwood will execute overwrite or deletion procedures on a best-effort basis and will complete such operations within thirty (30) calendar days unless a snapshot is explicitly tagged as "audit-retain" in which case the snapshot will be handled according to mutually-agreed exception procedures. Redwood will provide a redacted purge log and a signed attestation upon completion of deletion activities."

Please let us know which option maps best to your procurement needs. Per Daniel's ask, we will include a short note on cross-region cold archives (S3 Lifecycle transition caveats) and a sample redacted purge log.

I'll block Thu 30 Sep 10:00 PT for a quick 20-30 minute call — if that's still good, I'll send a calendar invite.

Best,
Marcus
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
